LRH1: LRH1 Photorealistic cinematic storyboard sheet for the opening of a luxury jewelry website, one single 16:9 image divided into a clean 3x3 grid of nine film frames with thin black gutters, small white numbers 1 to 9 in the top left corner of each frame. It must look like a Hollywood blockbuster title sequence or a high-end Cartier / Tiffany TV commercial: anamorphic lens, shallow depth of field, ultra sharp macro detail, dramatic contrast, real optics, light dust in the air, deep cobalt blue undertones in the shadows (#0f2563), pure white light. The jewelry store is called LUPENREIN (a store that sells diamonds, engagement rings and watches; NOT a workshop, no goldsmith tools, no flames). VERSION 1 'The floating ring'. Frame 1: total darkness, a single hard white beam of light falls from above into a black room with faint cobalt haze, dust particles glowing in the beam. Frame 2: a white gold diamond solitaire engagement ring floats in mid-air inside the beam, slowly rotating, nothing holds it. Frame 3: extreme macro of the six platinum prongs gripping the brilliant diamond, every polished edge razor sharp. Frame 4: macro of the diamond crown, the beam splits into spectral rainbow sparks across the facets. Frame 5: the ring turns, macro along the mirror-polished band, the beam glides over it like a reflection line. Frame 6: side silhouette of the floating ring against black, a thin rim light outlining it, sparks of light in the stone. Frame 7: the camera pulls back, the ring tiny in the beam in a vast dark space. Frame 8: the beam widens and the darkness opens like a curtain onto a bright white luxury jewelry gallery with glass vitrines and cobalt velvet. Frame 9: smartphone held vertically showing the floating ring in the beam with an elegant small title LUPENREIN and a scroll hint. Style: real high-end commercial cinematography, 8K macro photography, crisp facets with spectral fire (rainbow sparks), polished platinum reflections, consistent grading across all nine frames. Avoid: cartoon, illustration, CGI look, plastic look, cheap lens flares, clutter, text errors, logos, prices.
